mainTopic: A cow that was both borrowed and rented dies and the facts are unclear: the משנה's four rulings, and whether they refute רב נחמן on 'I don't know' claims.
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about a person who both borrowed and rented from the same owner, either one cow for different time periods or two separate cows. A borrower (שואל) pays even when the death was an unavoidable accident, but a renter (שוכר) does not. The משנה gives four cases. If the owner is sure it died while borrowed and the holder doesn't know, the holder pays. If the holder is sure it died while rented and the owner doesn't know, the holder is exempt. If each side is sure of the opposite, the renter swears and is exempt. If neither knows, they split the loss. The גמרא learns from the first case that someone who answers 'I don't know' to a sure money claim must pay. That seems to refute רב נחמן, who holds that such a person is פטור. The גמרא answers that רב נחמן agrees the unsure person pays when there is already an עסק שבועה, an oath situation, between the two sides, and the משנה is that kind of case. The גמרא then begins to define an oath situation using רבא's teaching, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Owner is sure it died while borrowed, the other side doesn't know: he pays
steps.stepSummary: The owner claims the cow died during the borrowed period. The person who had the cow says he doesn't know. He must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner says: 'It died during the hour it was borrowed.' The other one says: 'I don't know.' He is liable to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its first case. The owner insists the cow died while it was borrowed, the person holding it says 'I don't know,' and the ruling is that he must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל pays even for an unavoidable death, so if the death happened while the cow was borrowed, he owes. Here the owner makes a definite claim and the other side has nothing definite to answer with, so he is חייב. The גמרא will look closely at why: for רב נחמן, Step 7 explains he pays because an oath is already involved.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowed (the cow while it was on loan, free of charge)
And the other one (the opposing side)
I do not know
Liable (must pay)
A sure claim against an unsure one

steps.confusionAlert: The same person both borrowed and rented. The משנה covers two setups: one cow borrowed for part of the time and rented for part, or two cows, one borrowed and one rented. That is why the claims say either 'the borrowed one died' (which cow) or 'on the borrowed day / in the borrowed hour' (which time period).

phrases.english: [Or:] It died during the hour that it was borrowed.
And the other one says: I do not know. He is liable.
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is the person who had the cow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the owner's claim, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owner sure it died while borrowed, holder unsure: the holder pays.

steps.title: Renter is sure it died while rented, the owner doesn't know: he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: This is the reverse case. Now the holder is sure the cow died in the rented period, and the owner is unsure. The holder does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The renter says: 'The rented one died,' or 'It died on the rented day,' or 'It died in the rented hour.' The owner says: 'I don't know.' The renter is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the first case. The holder of the cow is the one who is sure, and he says it died while rented. The owner doesn't know, so the holder is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוכר does not pay for an unavoidable death. If the cow died in the rented period, nothing is owed. Once again the side with a definite claim beats the side that says 'I don't know.'

keyTerms.meaning: The renter (someone who pays to use the item)
Rented
Exempt (does not have to pay)

phrases.english: The renter says: The rented one died,
[or:] It died on the day that it was rented,
[or:] It died during the hour that it was rented.
And the other one says: I do not know. He is exempt.
phrases.notes: This time 'the other one' is the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 1, with the sure and unsure sides swapped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Renter sure it died while rented, owner unsure: the renter is exempt.

steps.title: Both sides are sure and they disagree: the renter swears and is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The owner is sure it died while borrowed, and the holder is sure it died while rented. The holder takes an oath and does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: One says 'borrowed' and the other says 'rented.' The renter swears that the rented one died.
steps.whatsHappening: Now both sides make a definite claim, but they contradict each other. The משנה rules that the renter swears it died while rented, and then he is free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side has the advantage of being sure, since both are. The money is in the holder's hands, so the owner can't simply take it from him. Instead the holder backs up his claim with a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... and that one (the two sides)
He shall swear (take an oath)

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אוֹמֵר: שְׁאוּלָה, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: שְׂכוּרָה –
phrases.english: This one says: borrowed, and that one says: rented.
phrases.notes: The owner says 'borrowed,' and the holder says 'rented.'

phrases.english: The renter swears that the rented one died.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: שְׁאוּלָה, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: שְׂכוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one sure side against one unsure side to two sure sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two opposite sure claims: the renter swears it died while rented and is exempt.

steps.title: Neither side knows: they split the loss
steps.stepSummary: Both the owner and the holder say 'I don't know.' The holder pays half the cow's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one says 'I don't know,' and that one says 'I don't know.' They divide.
steps.whatsHappening: In the last case, nobody knows when the cow died. The משנה rules יחלוקו: the loss is split down the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no sure claim on either side, so neither one wins. Since it could have been the borrowed period (he pays) or the rented period (he doesn't), the two sides share the doubt equally.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall divide (split the disputed amount)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four cases. Owner sure and holder unsure: the holder pays. Holder sure and owner unsure: the holder is exempt. Both sure: the renter swears and is exempt. Both unsure: they split it.
steps.whyThisMatters: These cases set up how a sure claim compares to an unsure one, and what to do when a doubt cannot be settled. The גמרא will take a close look at these rulings.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אוֹמֵר: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ –
phrases.english: This one says: I do not know, and that one says: I do not know.
They divide [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the set of four claim combinations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both unsure: the loss is split in half.

steps.title: Learning a general money rule from the cow case
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's case of the cow, the גמרא concludes: if someone says 'You owe me a מנה' and the other says 'I don't know,' he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Learn from this: if someone says, 'I have a מנה in your hand,' and the other says, 'I don't know,' he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the first case of the משנה (owner sure, holder unsure, holder pays) and turns it into a general rule for all money claims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the holder had to pay even though he only said 'I don't know.' The גמרא reasons that the same should be true for any loan claim. A sure claim beats an unsure answer, so the unsure person is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from a source)
A sum of money: one hundred dinars
I don't know
Liable, must pay

phrases.english: GEMARA: Learn from this:
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's first case, where the owner was sure and the holder said he didn't know (Step 1).

phrases.english: 'I have a maneh in your hand,'
phrases.notes: He means: 'You owe me a hundred dinars.'

phrases.english: and the other says: 'I don't know' — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general money-claim rule from the משנה's first case (Step 1).
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a defendant who says 'I don't know' to a sure claim is חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case: owner sure the cow died while borrowed, holder doesn't know, and the holder pays.

steps.title: This seems to refute רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests this rule disproves רב נחמן, who holds (with רבי יוחנן) that the 'I don't know' person is פטור, against רב הונא and רב יהודה, who say חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב נחמן? It was stated: 'I have a מנה in your hand,' and the other says 'I don't know.' רב הונא and רב יהודה say he is liable. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: the lesson from the משנה seems to directly contradict רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument. רב הונא and רב יהודה say the 'I don't know' person is חייב, and רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say he is פטור. Our משנה appears to side with רב הונא and רב יהודה. That would be a full refutation of רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (opens a suggested challenge)
A refutation, a strong disproof
Exempt, does not pay

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Nachman?
For it was stated: 'I have a maneh in your hand,'
and the other says: 'I don't know.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמְרִי: חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda say: he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי: פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan say: he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule learned in Step 5 to challenge רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that one who says 'I don't know' is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the unsure holder pay, which matches רב הונא and רב יהודה and goes against רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees when an oath is involved
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן himself said the 'I don't know' person is חייב when there is an עסק שבועה between them. The משנה's case is that kind of case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said: for example, where there is a matter of an oath between them. Here too, it is a case where there is a matter of an oath between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. He agrees the unsure person pays in a special situation, and our משנה is that situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's ruling of פטור is for a plain claim. When the defendant already owes a שבועה and can't take it because he doesn't know, he must pay. In the משנה the holder also owes an oath he can't swear, so he pays, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: As he said (quoting an earlier statement)
A situation where an oath is already required between the parties
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב נחמן changed his mind. He still says פטור in a plain 'I don't know' case. He only says חייב when an oath is already in the picture.

phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said:
for example, where there is a matter of an oath between them.
Here too —
it is a case where there is a matter of an oath between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by narrowing the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is a case of עסק שבועה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that anyone who says 'I don't know' always pays, against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a case where an oath is already involved, and רב נחמן agrees the unsure person pays in such a case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רב נחמן's ruling of פטור for plain 'I don't know' claims. It also shows that being unable to swear an owed oath leads to paying.

steps.title: What counts as an oath situation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what an עסק שבועה looks like and starts to answer by pointing to רבא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'a matter of an oath'? Like רבא's teaching,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of עסק שבועה and begins its answer with רבא. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 7 depends on the term עסק שבועה, so the גמרא now asks what exactly it means. It introduces רבא's teaching, which will spell out the case, as the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Like the teaching of רבא

phrases.english: What is the case of 'a matter of an oath'?
Like Rava's teaching,
